judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The hero photo beside the CAO Hub heading (not a link). The crop and the screenshot show a young woman with curly hair in a pink hoodie, arms folded, in a campus interior: a student, which is what the alternative says, so the claim that it describes something the image does not show is false. 'Image of' is redundant wording, but the alternative serves the photo's illustrative purpose, so 1.1.1 is met. The live HTML has the same img and alt, and the screenshot is fully styled, so the capture does not differ.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The promo photo in the Build Your Prospectus section, not a link. The crop shows a person, out of focus, holding a smartphone towards the camera with the ATU Digital Prospectus page on screen, exactly what the alternative says; it is an accurate, adequate text alternative, so 1.1.1 is met and Rampa missed nothing. The live HTML has the same img and alt.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The photo inside the 'Find Your Course' card link (the link also holds the visible text, and its computed name is 'image of two students studying Find Your Course'). The crop shows two students at a desk in a study space, one smiling and one from behind, so the alternative matches the picture and the claim is false. Because the link text gives the purpose, the photo is supplementary; a null alt would be tidier (H2), but a short accurate description is not a 1.1.1 failure. The live HTML is identical.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The photo inside the 'Join Our Community' card link. The crop shows three young people walking along a path with red tulips at the sides, a modern building with large windows and a lawn behind them, which is the alternative word for word, so the claim is false. The link text carries the purpose; the alternative is accurate, if long, and the image meets 1.1.1. The live HTML has the same alt.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Study' item of the Primary navigation: an a href='#' with aria-expanded='false' (exposed as collapsed) that opens the Study mega menu (data-menuid 001, whose hidden list holds Study at ATU, All Courses, Apprenticeships, Undergraduate/CAO and more). It is a disclosure toggle, not a link to a destination; its purpose, to open the Study section's menu, is clear from the text 'Study', its collapsed state and its place in the Primary navigation list, beside Student Life, Research, Connect and About. The claim that nothing tells where it goes treats it as a page link; 2.4.4 is met. Using a link with href='#' as a button is at most a 4.1.2 role question, not a 2.4.4 failure. The live HTML has the same markup.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The photo inside the 'Here for You' card link (student support). The crop shows a student in a hijab at a desk looking up at another young woman bending over to talk to her, with architectural drawings pinned on the wall: students in an interior architecture studio, as the alternative says. It does not mention that one is helping the other, but that detail is not essential to an illustrative photo in a link whose visible text gives its purpose, so the alternative does not leave out what the image conveys there, and 1.1.1 is met. The live HTML is identical.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The photo inside the 'Academic Supports' card link. The crop shows a student at an iMac and a woman (a lecturer) pointing at the screen, in a computer lab: a student, a lecturer and a Mac lab, so the claim that the alternative describes something the image does not show is false. 'Student-Lecturer-Mac-Lab' looks like a media-library title, with hyphens, but its words do describe the picture, unlike a camera filename, and the link text carries the purpose; I do not count it as an F30 failure. If an auditor did, that would be a reason the claim does not name, so the label would still be false_positive. The live HTML is identical.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Student Hub' link in the Utility navigation, which goes to https://studenthub.atu.ie/. The text names the destination, the Student Hub site, so its purpose can be determined from the link text alone. The other links named 'Student Hub' (in the hidden Student Life menu, the mobile menu and the mobile utility area) all go to studenthub.atu.ie, with or without the trailing slash, which is the same resource, so R1 finds no failure. 2.4.4 is met and Rampa missed nothing. The live page has the same links.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The photo inside the 'Scholarships' card link. The crop (the card shows only part of the photo) shows three people at a desk in a bright, open study area with lights overhead: two seated with devices in front of them and one standing holding a grey notebook or folder. The alternative matches the scene; small details such as whether the devices are tablets are not 'something the image does not show', and the link text carries the purpose. The claim is false and 1.1.1 is met. The live HTML is identical.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Computing' link in the subject list under Explore Our Courses, which goes to the Study Computing page (heading 'Computing', undergraduate computing courses). Its list item holds only 'Computing', and the heading just before it in the DOM is an empty h2 (class 'title', no text, also on the live page), so the context adds nothing. The link text alone still names the destination's subject, matching the page's heading, which is enough for 2.4.4 (Understanding 2.4.4 does not require the document's full name). No other link on the page is named 'Computing'. 2.4.4 is met. The empty heading is a separate 1.3.1 matter.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The photo inside the 'Undergraduate Entry Routes' card link has alt='53316623680_84c94b74e5_k', a Flickr-style photo ID, which is the failure F30 describes (a filename or placeholder used as the text alternative). The crop shows two smiling young women holding large ATU letters at an event, and the ID says none of this. Because the alt is not null, the link's computed name becomes '53316623680_84c94b74e5_k Undergraduate Entry Routes', so the ID is read out to screen reader users. It fails 1.1.1 whether the photo is treated as informative (no equivalent) or as decorative (it should then have a null alt, not a meaningless string). The claim that the alternative names a label rather than what the image conveys points at exactly this. The live HTML has the same alt.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The photo inside the "What's New at ATU" card link. The crop shows two young women leaning over patterned fabric on a worktable, with a dress form behind them, in a textiles studio. That is a student and a lecturer (or two people) looking at textiles, as the alternative says, so the claim is false. The alternative is accurate and the link text gives the purpose, so 1.1.1 is met. The live HTML is identical.
